correctness.rationale: For all finite m>=1, positive A_j, nu_j, gamma and omega_0, the stationary spectrum equals f(omega^2)=B(z)/P(z), B=sum_j(2A_j nu_j)/(z+nu_j^2), P=(omega_0^2-z)^2+4gamma^2 z>0. The sign of its derivative is G=P B'-P' B. If c=4gamma^2-2omega_0^2>=0 then G<0. For c<0, G'=2Z H with H=d+c z-2z E_z[t]-E_z[t^2], and distribution p_j proportional a_j/(z+t_j)^3 shifts toward larger t_j; H strictly decreases, hence G has at most one maximum and at most two positive zeros. G(infinity)=-3 sum a_j<0; at most one positive off-center maximum, and by evenness at most three global-frequency peaks. Independently reconstructed single-rate polynomial 3z^2-39z/10+2451/2500 with roots 0.3406458 and 0.9593542 in the strict three-peak example. Continuity preserves strict peaks under arbitrarily many sufficiently weak extra channels; finite random trials are not the proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge O PASS for the arbitrary-positive-mixture Stieltjes derivative shape theorem. Masoliver and Porrà derive the transfer-spectrum and classify single exponential noise, including a three-peak regime, which are acknowledged prior results. The inspected 1993 source gives no arbitrary-m positive-mixture theorem, and positive summation of unimodal terms alone is not a valid implication. Search covered OU superpositions and general oscillator resonance terminology; no dominating result was verified, but a general total-positivity/Stieltjes variation theorem could implicitly cover the same conclusion.

value.rationale: A rate-independent ceiling on observable spectral resonances for a second-order scalar system under arbitrarily many positive relaxation channels constrains which multi-peak observations can be attributed to colored forcing alone. It is a natural structural spectral bound (not a tiny numeric check), sharp already with one channel, with a practical distinction between multiple forcing scales and multiple mechanical modes.
